skill.name: quality-gates
skill.description: Run structured quality gates for JavaScript and TypeScript projects before commits, pull requests, or deployments.
skill.summary: Guide lint, type, test, build, audit, and Git checks before release.
skill.author: AI-Vibe-Prompts

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown formatting or inline code examples, not Ruby backtick execution. The remaining confirmed issues are legitimate quality-gate commands that run package scripts, modify files, install tooling, or may expose secret matches. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Project scripts and package manager commands can execute repository code.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before npm, pnpm, npx, build, test, and install commands. Show the exact command first.

remediation.issue: Secret searches may print matched secret values into model context.
remediation.suggestion: Use redacted secret scanning output. Report only file names, line numbers, and match types, not secret values.

remediation.issue: Automatic fix and cleanup commands can modify or delete files.
remediation.suggestion: Run non-mutating checks by default. Ask before fix commands, audit fixes, cleanup commands, or package installation.

remediation.issue: The hook bypass example can normalize skipping quality checks.
remediation.suggestion: Limit no-verify guidance to emergencies. Require an explicit user request before suggesting it.

content.value_statement: Code changes need consistent validation before commits and deployments. This skill guides lint, type, test, build, security, and Git checks in one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Detects common JavaScript and TypeScript lint tools such as ESLint and Biome.
Runs or recommends project type checking through package scripts or TypeScript.
Finds test files and runs common test frameworks such as Vitest and Jest.
Checks production builds and expected build artifact directories.
Runs dependency audit checks and staged Git checks for secrets and large files.
Reports gate status, failures, durations, and follow-up recommendations.
limitations: It is optimized for JavaScript and TypeScript projects using npm or pnpm.
It depends on project scripts and tools already being installed or installable.
Shell commands can modify files and should be reviewed before execution.
Security checks focus on dependency audits and simple staged diff scans.

use_cases.title: Validate a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Run linting, type checks, tests, and build checks before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Candidate
use_cases.description: Run the comprehensive gate set before deployment to reduce build, test, and dependency risk.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Checks
use_cases.description: Define a repeatable quality workflow for commits, pushes, and CI pipeline readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation after a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Level 1 quality gates for this project. Summarize lint and type check results with any required fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Before Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the pre-commit quality gates on my staged changes. Report blockers, warnings, and the safest next action.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the comprehensive quality gates for this release candidate. Include tests, build verification, dependency audit, and Git checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Gate Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and propose a quality gate policy for commits, pushes, and deployments. Respect existing scripts and thresholds.

output_examples.input: Run quality gates before I commit this feature.
output_examples.output: The skill reports which gates passed, which failed, and the exact files or checks needing attention before commit.

output_examples.input: Check whether this release is ready to deploy.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes test, build, audit, and Git status, then lists release blockers and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Set up a repeatable quality process for this repository.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes fast, standard, and comprehensive gate levels based on the detected project tools.

best_practices: Run fast gates first, then continue to slower checks only after critical failures are resolved.
Review each shell command before execution in sensitive or production repositories.
Use project-defined scripts and thresholds when they are available.
anti_patterns: Running automatic fixes across unrelated files without user approval.
Treating warning-only complexity checks as release blockers without team policy.
Using hook bypass commands as a normal commit workflow.

faq.question: What projects does this skill fit best?
faq.answer: It fits JavaScript and TypeScript projects that use npm, pnpm, ESLint, Biome, Vitest, Jest, or similar tools.

faq.question: Does it change files automatically?
faq.answer: It can recommend or run fix commands, but users should approve commands that modify files.

faq.question: Can it replace a CI pipeline?
faq.answer: No. It helps run local checks and design gates, but CI remains the source of shared enforcement.

faq.question: Does it find all security issues?
faq.answer: No. It checks dependencies and simple staged diff patterns, but it is not a full security review.

faq.question: Does it support non-JavaScript projects?
faq.answer: Support is limited. The documented commands and detection logic focus on JavaScript and TypeScript workflows.

faq.question: Why should commands be reviewed first?
faq.answer: Package scripts and install commands can run repository code or modify files, so review reduces accidental risk.
